definition: Branch coverage inside the function's span, 0.0 to 1.0. With no branches it is statement coverage, and with no statements invoked-or-not (1.0 or 0.0). Python and/or add to ccn but give coverage.py no branch arc. untested, no-lane and cc-only rows read 0.0.
readme: branch coverage inside the function's span | falls back to statement coverage | with no statements to invoked-or-not
context: share of a function's branches | statements | invoked-or-not | no branch arc
agent_json: branch coverage in the span, 0.0 to 1.0 | statement coverage | invoked-or-not | no branch arc
mcp: branch coverage | statement coverage when the span has no branches | invoked-or-not | no branch arc

definition: ccn^2 x (1 - cov)^3 + ccn: the C.R.A.P. formula of Savoia and Evans, with cov as a fraction. A cc-only row scores ccn.
readme: crap = ccn^2 * (1 - cov)^3 + ccn | crap = ccn
sarif: crap score above the scope ceiling | crap {crap:.1f}

definition: Why a coverage number is there or not: measured (a lane artifact spoke about the function), untested (a lane covers the scope and its artifact is silent on the function, or cannot tell it apart from a function sharing its lines), no-lane (no lane covers the scope), cc-only (the scope sets coverage_optional).
agent_json: measured | untested | no-lane | cc-only | cannot tell apart

definition: The first move that can lower the score: decompose when ccn > ceiling, else ok when crap <= ceiling, else split-lines when another function shares the span or a Python def's body starts on its signature's last line, else add-tests.
readme: decompose | split-lines | add-tests | ok | ccn > ceiling | crap <= ceiling

definition: Maximum nesting depth, read off crapkit's cognitive pass in every language: one level for the body of each if, else if, else, loop, switch and catch, and in Python of each elif, except, match statement and comprehension for; none for a logical operator, a case label, try, finally, with or a nested def.
agent_json: maximum nesting depth | a flat function of seven ifs reads 1 | three nested loops read 3 | an if inside a with inside an if reads 2

definition: Lines of code without comments: a line counts when it holds code, so comment-only and blank lines do not.
agent_json: non-comment lines of code | comment-only lines and blank lines do not count

definition: The function's parameter count. A brief's params lists the same parameters in declaration order, so scored.params is its length.
agent_json: declaration order | scored.params is the count

definition: The scope's effective ceiling: the highest CRAP a function may carry, and so also the highest ccn. A scope's own target overrides the [crapkit] target.
context: highest crap a function may carry | complexity limit

definition: Which finding a verify --json findings item is: unreadable_name, gate_violation, unread_file, ratchet_regression, new_failure, diff_uncovered or overridden, one row each of verify.FINDING_KINDS. Items come in that order, the exit order, and inside a kind in the order its 0.8.1 list gives them.
context: unreadable name, gate violation, unread file, ratchet regression, new failure, diff uncovered and overridden, in that order
agent_json: unreadable_name, gate_violation, unread_file, ratchet_regression, new_failure, diff_uncovered or overridden
declaration: unreadable_name, gate_violation, unread_file, ratchet_regression, new_failure, diff_uncovered or overridden

definition: True when the item fails the verdict: its kind fires an exit code and the verdict holds it. A diff_uncovered item fails only past diff_uncovered_max, and an overridden item never fails.
context: whether it fails the verdict | overridden is a report and fails nothing
agent_json: true when the item fails the verdict | fails only past diff_uncovered_max | an overridden one never does
declaration: true when this item fails the verdict | fails only past diff_uncovered_max | an overridden one never does

definition: The exit code a failing item fires: 3 unreadable_name, 6 gate_violation and unread_file, 7 ratchet_regression, 8 new_failure, 9 diff_uncovered; null when fails is false. The first failing item's exit_code is verify's exit, which is 0 when no item fails.
readme: a scoped file whose name is not UTF-8 | Gate violation | Ratchet regression | New test failures | Diff-coverage ceiling breached
context: the first failing kind present sets verify's exit: 3, then 6, 7, 8 and 9
agent_json: null when fails is false | the first item whose fails is true names verify's exit
declaration: 3 unreadable_name, 6 gate_violation and unread_file, 7 ratchet_regression, 8 new_failure, 9 diff_uncovered | null when fails is false | the first failing item's exit_code is verify's exit

definition: True for a gate_violation, the one kind an --override can grant. An override grants nothing while an item of a kind that refuses one is present: unreadable_name, unread_file, ratchet_regression or new_failure.
agent_json: true for a gate_violation, the one kind an --override can grant | grants nothing while an item of a kind that refuses one is present
declaration: true for a gate_violation, the one kind an --override can grant | grants nothing while an item of a kind that refuses one is present

definition: True when the item's file has uncommitted edits, staged or not, or git does not track it; a new_failure is dirty when its test id names such a file. verify's diff holds tracked files only, so only a new_failure's test file can be untracked.
declaration: uncommitted edits or git does not track it | for a new_failure, when its test id names such a file

definition: The label of the rule an item stands for, the words the pull-request comment opens its verdict with: complexity gate for a gate_violation or an unread_file, ratchet regressions, new test failures, diff-coverage ceiling, unreadable name, and override for an overridden item.
readme: the rule it stands for | complexity gate | ratchet regressions | new test failures | diff-coverage ceiling
agent_json: the label of the item's rule | pull-request comment
declaration: the label of the item's rule | complexity gate (gate_violation, unread_file), ratchet regressions, new test failures, diff-coverage ceiling, unreadable name or override

definition: How many changed lines no lane ran, every one, where findings lists the first 50 as diff_uncovered items. A changed file no lane artifact mentions counts every line of its functions.
readme: more changed lines than that never ran | a changed file no lane artifact mentions counts every line of its functions
agent_json: every changed line no test ran
declaration: changed lines no test ran, every one | findings lists the first 50

definition: The ceiling diff_uncovered_count is judged against: past it, each diff_uncovered item fails with exit 9. null when the repo set none, and then no uncovered line fails.
readme: diff_uncovered_max is set and more changed lines than that never ran
agent_json: the ceiling diff_uncovered_count is judged against | null when the repo set none
declaration: the ceiling diff_uncovered_count is judged against | null when the repo set none
